# Radio

One choice in a `RadioGroup`, with its label to its right. Pass the choices as the group's `options` unless you need a layout they cannot express, such as a choice with a rich description; then render `Radio` children.

```tsx
import { Radio } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/radio-group/radio-group";
```

## Example

```tsx
<RadioGroup legend="Size" name="size">
  <Radio value="small" label="Small" description="Serves 2." />
  <Radio value="large" label="Large" description="Serves 6." />
</RadioGroup>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `Checkbox` inside a `CheckboxGroup` instead when several choices may be picked.

## Props

Type: `RadioProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement. Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Supporting text under the label, read after it through `aria-describedby`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables this one radio; the arrow keys skip it. |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Hides the label visually; screen readers still read it as the radio's name. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The choice's name, shown to the right of the radio. Required: every control needs a name. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | The radio element, a `<span role="radio">`. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What the group submits when this radio is picked, and the group's `value` then. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `checked`: Not a prop. The group's `value` picks the radio: `<RadioGroup value="small">`.
- `name`: Not a prop. The group's `name` applies to every radio: `<RadioGroup name="size">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
